title: “Artificial Enhancements” · Tickle College of Engineering
description: The Tickle College of Engineering featured the lab's work on AI teammates: AI agents built to act as genuine collaborators rather than chatbots, and the ARO-funded effort to detect and recover from compromised teammates across manufacturing, nuclear energy, disaster recovery, and healthcare.

title: “Detecting Compromised AI Teammates” · Tennessee Engineer
description: Tennessee Engineer magazine profiled the lab's Army Research Office–funded study of how to prevent, recognize, and quickly recover from attacks on AI teammates before they undermine human-AI team performance.

title: “Schelble's ARO Agreement to Help Create More Secure Human-AI Teams”
description: Tickle College of Engineering news on the lab's Army Research Office cooperative agreement on preventing and recovering from compromised AI teammates (also carried by EurekAlert!), including how human-AI teams can recognize when an AI may have been attacked.

title: Invited seminar at UTK Psychology & Neuroscience
description: Dr. Schelble delivered "Human-AI Teaming: The Importance of Human-AI Complementarity" at the University of Tennessee Psychology & Neuroscience Department Seminar.

title: New PACM HCI article on AI teammates in transition phases
description: "A Mixed Methods Approach to Analyzing the Role of AI Teammates in Transition Phases" appears in the Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction.

title: Complementarity framework published in PNAS Nexus
description: "Toward a Science of Human-AI Teaming for Decision-Making: A Complementarity Framework", a multi-institution collaboration including Carnegie Mellon, is out in PNAS Nexus.

title: National Academies webinar on human-AI team performance
description: Dr. Schelble presented "Performance Optimization in Human-AI Teams" to the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine Board on Human-Systems Integration.

title: AI on the Battlefield · West Point
description: Invited talk "Mitigating the Risks of Compromised AI Teammates" at the AI on the Battlefield Workshop, United States Military Academy at West Point.

title: Technical Advisory Panel on AI in warfare
description: Dr. Schelble delivered a Human-Machine Teaming Deep Dive for the Technical Advisory Panel on the Use of AI Systems in Warfare.

title: ACM TiiS Featured Article honors
description: "I Know This Looks Bad, But I Can Explain" was selected as a 2023 & 2024 Featured Article for ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems.

title: ARO funds ARCS Lab research on compromised AI teammates
description: The Army Research Office awarded a cooperative agreement to study preventing, identifying, and mitigating compromised AI teammates using shared situation awareness and mental model accuracy.

title: Invited talks at CMU and UT Austin
description: Dr. Schelble spoke at Carnegie Mellon's AI Institute for Societal Decision Making and at the University of Texas at Austin's NSF NRT seminar series on ethics and team cognition in human-AI teams.

title: ARCS Lab launches at the University of Tennessee
description: Dr. Schelble joined UTK Industrial & Systems Engineering as Assistant Professor and founded the AI & Robotics for Collaborative Systems (ARCS) Lab.

title: Most Outstanding Graduate Student, Clemson HCC
description: Recognized as the Most Outstanding Graduate Student in Clemson University's Human-Centered Computing PhD program.

title: Invited industry talk at RTX
description: "Human-AI Teaming: Ethics, Trust, & Shared Knowledge" presented at RTX (Raytheon Technologies), East Hartford, CT.

title: Best JCEDM Article of 2022
description: "Exploring the Relationship Between Ethics and Trust in Human-AI Teaming" named Best Journal of Cognitive Engineering and Decision Making Article of 2022.

title: Best Paper Honorable Mention at ACM GROUP
description: "Let's Think Together!" received a Best Paper Honorable Mention at the ACM International Conference on Supporting Group Work.

title: Best Overall Paper at HAI 2020
description: "Invoking Principles of Groupware to Develop and Evaluate Present and Future Human-Agent Teams" won Best Overall Paper at the 8th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction.
